slides.title: Ballon d'Or night, taken apart.
slides.sub: Bayern had one hero. Barça had twelve nominees. Two playbooks.

slides.body: The profile itself became content: Bayern's own comment, “Just updated our bio 😏”, drew 2.2k likes.
slides.tip: Hypothesis: a small in-joke gives fans something to reply to.

slides.title: One hero, five surfaces
slides.body: A winner graphic (781.6k likes), a reel (2.2M), a golden Allianz Arena collab (342k), a new bio and a day-after callback to “never win a trophy” (251k).
slides.tip: Hypothesis: the callback works because it answers a doubt fans already know.

callouts.l: likes on the “three years” stat post

slides.body: Barça framed Yamal's award as a streak: “2024, 2025, 2026…” Here the plain award photo got more likes than the stat post.

slides.title: Twelve nominees, one story
slides.body: A nominees reel the day before (265k likes), a “Gala ready” reel (626k), then award-night posts up to 1.9M. Likes grew as the night got closer.
slides.tip: Hypothesis: the build-up warmed the audience for the night itself.

slides.body: No statement after finishing third: a short video with his partner, captioned with one pink heart.
slides.tip: Hypothesis: with no words, fans wrote the story themselves.

slides.title: Viral, not his record
slides.body: It is 7th by views among his last 11 TikToks (top: 167.1M, 30 Sep), but more than double his two previous posts (37.7M and 33M).
slides.tip: Judge a viral moment against the account's own baseline, not in isolation.

slides.body: Data as content: a ranking to argue about. Top comments: “Where's CR7?”, “Where is the points?”
slides.tip: Hypothesis: a list invites debate about who is missing.

slides.title: Match the story to your squad: one hero gets depth, many nominees get a shared identity.
Use your own surfaces: a bio change, a collab post and a day-after callback cost almost nothing.
